records.reason: V23 remains Human Accepted for physical folder-stack behavior, while V53 is the published integrated atlas/navigation surface to preserve visually.
The earlier V23-derived integration caused a visible regression and is retained only as technical evidence.

records.old: shared/shell/v1 visible shell mounted over V53
records.reason: V53 already owns the terminal, iframe and return tooth; a second visible shell would duplicate UI, Back and focus ownership.

records.old: Touch-First V2 mounted on V53 viewport
records.new: Touch-First V2 opt-in for page/widget consumers
records.reason: V53 already owns its approved one-axis pointer physics; a second adapter would create competing gesture ownership.
The outer iframe is useful for same-origin injection tests but adds a browser boundary and is not the final human product surface.
V53 loads tree.json and pages.json separately; a stable build string alone cannot prove that the semantic route graph is unchanged.
Two concurrently staged transactions can otherwise share the same next revision and silently overwrite each other.
V1 is in-memory and lacks durable indexing, privacy inheritance, supersession, watermarks and reopenability; those are explicit Part 2 work.
